title: Comparative Dynamic Features of Apo and Bound MDM2 Protein Reveal the Mechanism of Inhibitor Recognition for Anti-Cancer Activity.
authors: I El Habbash, Aisha; El Rashedy, Ahmed; Soliman, Mahmoud E S
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子动力学模拟研究MDM2蛋白与小分子抑制剂的结合机制，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作，但对象为蛋白-小分子而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA体系，与本课题关联度低。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mouse Double Minute 2 Homolog (MDM2) oncogenic protein is the principal cellular antagonist of the p53 tumor suppressor gene. Restoration of p53 activity by inhibiting the MDM2-P53 interactions at the molecular level has become the cornerstone of cancer research due to its promising anticancer effects. Natural medicinal products possess various chemical structures and represent an essential source for drug discovery. alpha-Mangostin (AM) and gambogic acid (G250) are plant-derived compounds that showed inhibitory effects on MDM2-P53 interactions in vitro and in vivo. METHODS: Despite the many clinical studies which performed deeper insight about the molecular understanding of the structural mechanisms exhibited by alpha-Mangostin and Gambogic acid-binding to MDM2 remains critical. In this study, comparative molecular dynamics simulations were performed for each Apo and bound p53 and MDM2 proteins to shed light on the MDM2-p53 interactions and get a better understanding of the inhibition mechanisms. RESULTS: Results revealed atomistic interaction of AM and G250 within the MDM2-p53 interaction cleft. Both compounds mediate the interaction between the alpha-helix motifs of the p53 amino-terminal domain, which caused a significant separation between orthogonally opposed residues, specifically Lys8 and Gly47 residues of the p53 and MDM2, respectively. Contrasting changes in magnitudes were observed in per-residue fluctuation on AM and G250 (~0.04 nm and ~2.3 nm, respectively). The Radius of gyration (~0.03 nm and 0.04 nm, respectively), C-alpha deviations (~0.06 nm and 0.1 nm, respectively). The phenolic group of AM was found to establish hydrogen interactions with Glu28 and His96 residues of MDM2. The trioxahexacyclo-ring of G250 also forms hydrogen bond interactions with Lys51 and Leu26 residues of MDM2. CONCLUSION: Utilizing the information provided on the inhibitory binding mode adopted by each compound in this study may further assist in the tailored designs for cancer therapeutics.
abstract_zh: 背景：小鼠双微体2同源物（MDM2）致癌蛋白是p53肿瘤抑制基因的主要细胞拮抗剂。通过分子水平抑制MDM2-P53相互作用来恢复p53活性，已成为癌症研究的基石，因其具有前景的抗癌效果。天然药用产物具有多样的化学结构，是药物发现的重要来源。α-倒捻子素（AM）和藤黄酸（G250）是植物来源的化合物，在体外和体内均显示出对MDM2-P53相互作用的抑制效果。方法：尽管许多临床研究对α-倒捻子素和藤黄酸与MDM2结合的结构机制进行了更深入的分子理解，但这一方面仍至关重要。在本研究中，对Apo和结合的p53及MDM2蛋白分别进行了比较分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，以阐明MDM2-p53相互作用并更好地理解抑制机制。结果：结果揭示了AM和G250在MDM2-p53相互作用裂隙内的原子级相互作用。两种化合物介导了p53氨基末端结构域α-螺旋基序之间的相互作用，导致正交相对残基（特别是p53的Lys8和MDM2的Gly47残基）之间发生显著分离。在AM和G250的逐残基波动中观察到幅度对比变化（分别约为0.04 nm和2.3 nm）。回转半径（分别约为0.03 nm和0.04 nm），C-α偏差（分别约为0.06 nm和0.1 nm）。发现AM的酚基与MDM2的Glu28和His96残基建立氢键相互作用。G250的三氧杂六环结构也与MDM2的Lys51和Leu26残基形成氢键相互作用。结论：利用本研究中每种化合物所采用的抑制结合模式信息，可能进一步有助于癌症治疗药物的定制设计。
